Q1: Sodium silicate exhibits known significant hazards (Tier 1) for oral, dermal/eye, and organ/systemic exposures, along with potential inhalation hazards (Tier 2). It is categorized with low to moderate environmental hazards (Tier 3), but data are currently deficient (Tier 4) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards, and endocrine disruption.
Q2: Sodium silicate is not currently identified on specific "Lists of Concern." The absence of such listings may, in part, reflect existing data deficiencies for certain hazard classes, including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards, and endocrine disruption.
Q3: Sodium silicate is well-characterized, boasting 30,000 scientific references, which is considerably above the median for characterized chemicals. Its molecular formula is specific, and it is not classified as a UVCB or an incompletely defined substance, although two hazard classes currently lack sufficient data.
